summary: Staging API keys were replayed as production keys causing a one-off embedding charge
description:
Issue summary: Customer noticed a single, high-value embedding invoice line dated 2026-03-08 for ~1.2M tokens (~$4,200) attributed to their production org. Customer insists the load originated from a staging service that should be excluded from billing.

Impact: One unexpected invoice line causing a customer-facing billing surprise and an open support escalation with finance. Customer paused automatic renewals pending clarification.

Environment: LexiQ Health production org (org_id: org_lexiq_prod). Requests in question appear under api_key prefixes matching their historical staging naming convention (stg-*) but were recorded under the production org in postback logs. Region: us-east-1. Model: text-embedding-3-large.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Nightly batch job on 2026-03-08 ran an internal staging reindex using keys named stg-reindex-01 -> reported 2026-03-09 when invoice generated.
2) Customer verifies the key was a staging key that had been deleted on 2026-02-25 and should not have been active.
3) Customer sees the usage line on the monthly invoice for period ending 2026-03-08.

Observed billing lines: Invoice ID INV-LEXIQ-20260308 line item: text-embedding-3-large, 1,204,320 tokens, charge $4,212.48, note: "metered usage (postback reconciler v2)".

Expected behavior: Staging keys that are flagged as non-billable (stg- prefix & tag:environment=staging) should be ignored by the billing pipeline and not attributed to production orgs.

Initial hypothesis: Postback reconciler v2 introduced a relaxed key-to-org mapping regex during the 2026-02-20 change, which may have allowed deleted / staging key signatures to remap to the most recent matching org.

Immediate customer request: Temporary reversal of the invoice line while we investigate, and an explanation of why deleted staging keys were billed.

investigation_notes: Checked reconciler v1 vs v2 behavior: v1 used strong key->org mapping table; v2 introduced incremental reconciliation with compaction and a last-writer-wins mapping which can lose 'deleted' state during compaction.
SRE traced the exact partition and found gap in metadata refresh for keys with stg- prefix between 2026-02-24 and 2026-02-26 due to an out-of-order compaction window.

Confirmed the usage batch from 2026-03-08 included replayed events originating from an internal LexiQ staging job which submitted requests before the key deletion but the reconciler processed them after compaction removed the deletion flag.
No evidence of malicious activity or key leakage. The root cause is an ordering bug in compaction + reconciliation heuristics.
Finance approves provisional credit pending final RCA; rollback risk low as reconcile database will be updated and audit will confirm effective non-billing for deleted keys in range.
resolution: Provisional credit issued (CR-LEXIQ-20260311) to cover the one-off charge. Engineering patch to reconciler merged (PR #4112) and scheduled for canary deploy 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC to fix key-to-org attribution by honoring explicit key metadata and treating deleted-state keys as non-billable. Post-deploy audit task INT-9042 created to run a re-reconciliation for 2026-02-20 through 2026-03-10 and to identify any other affected invoices. Finance will follow up to finalize any permanent invoice adjustments or communication. Customer notified and will receive a confirmation email once audit completes.
